subject: Re: Private deployment: maintenance windows, operator access, and contract language
messages:
From: Thomas Blake <thomas.blake@helioshealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Carol Nguyen <carol.nguyen@helioshealth.com>, procure@helioshealth.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: maintenance windows, operator access, and contract language

Hi Alex / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Helios wants to straighten out a couple items before we open an SOW: specifically maintenance/patching practices for an on-prem air-gapped install, the expected operator access model, and a proposal for SLA language around maintenance windows and emergency patches. A few concrete questions: 

1) For air-gapped customers, do you deliver a signed offline patch bundle or is it a scripted pull from our network? How do we verify integrity after transfer?
2) What is the typical SLA for applying critical security patches in an isolated environment? Do you commit to an operator-assisted install window (e.g., 72 hours after delivery)?
3) Can Redwood provide operator training and an offline runbook as part of the initial engagement? If so, how many sessions and are they billed separately?
4) We have a standard clause that limits support hours to business hours for maintenance unless an emergency SLA is invoked — is that compatible with your on-prem support model?

We want to capture these in contract language (or a mutual action plan) so the legal team can move fast. Happy to take a quick call tomorrow if that's easier.

Thanks,
Thomas
Thomas Blake
Head of Procurement, Helios Health
procure@helioshealth.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Blake <thomas.blake@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2029 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: maintenance windows, operator access, and contract language

Hi Thomas — great questions, and thanks for laying them out. I pulled together a short summary and attached a one-page SLA/maintenance note that we typically use for private/on-prem customers. High level answers below; happy to expand in a call.

1) Offline package + signatures: For air-gapped installs we deliver a signed tarball (SHA-256) plus a detached signature from our release key. Customers verify the checksum locally before installation. For larger customers we can also provide a sealed USB distribution or a hashed artifact on a carrier — all options are documented in the runbook. (See attachment: private_deploy_sla_summary.pdf)

2) Critical patching SLA: We treat critical security fixes as a 72-hour response window for delivering the patch artifact and instructions. For air-gapped sites that requires coordination for delivery; our standard is: deliver artifact within 72 hours, and target operator-assisted install within 7 calendar days unless otherwise agreed in SOW. We can shorten that timeline for an upgraded support package.

3) Operator training + runbook: We include a baseline operator onboarding (2 x 90m sessions) as part of initial Private deployment. Additional sessions or tailored training are quoted separately. We deliver an offline runbook (PDF) and a signed SBOM snapshot with the initial bundle.

4) Support hours: Our default on-prem support is 8x5 business-hours with emergency 24/7 escalation for severity-1 incidents if a support add-on is purchased. For maintenance windows, we propose a standard monthly maintenance window (2 hours) for non-critical updates; emergency patches are handled per the critical patching SLA above.

Next steps I propose: 
- I can share a short mutual action plan that maps procurement/legal asks to contract language and SOW items.
- If you want accelerated patch timelines or 24/7 operator install support for emergency windows, we can include that in the MAP as an optional line item.

If that all looks reasonable, I can schedule a 30-min call with Vanessa and our Ops PM (Priya) to finalize recommended clause language.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0191

Cc: Carol Nguyen <carol.nguyen@helioshealth.com>, procure@helioshealth.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2029 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: maintenance windows, operator access, and contract language

Alex — appreciate the fast response and the summary. A few follow ups to clarify legal's immediate asks: 

• Verification: Can you include sample verification commands and an example of the signed artifact verification in the runbook we send to legal? They want something they can paste into an internal runbook.
• SLA language: Legal wants explicit timing: "Redwood will deliver the patch artifact within seventy-two (72) hours of a Severity 1 security advisory and provide operator install guidance. Customer-installation target shall be within seven (7) calendar days of artifact delivery unless otherwise agreed." Are you able to accept that exact phrasing or do you need edits?
• Training: Please confirm whether the two 90-minute sessions are live remote sessions and whether recordings are provided for internal knowledge base use.
• Costs: Quick confirmation of whether runbook + signed SBOM are included in the initial deployment fee or if they are listed as professional services line items.

Would also like to loop in our CFO (Carol) on cost/term questions; CC'd here. If possible, Vanessa or Priya, can you map these items into a row-level MAP so procurement can sign off?

Thanks,
Thomas

Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: maintenance windows, operator access, and contract language

Priya / Alex — forwarding Thomas' note and Alex's summary. Priya, can you drop these into a quick MAP spreadsheet and propose exact clause language for the 72-hour / 7-day items? I drafted suggested wording in column C of the attached file and flagged costs in column F.

Suggested clause (high level):
"Redwood will deliver a signed patch artifact within seventy-two (72) hours of identification of a Severity 1 security advisory. Redwood will provide installation instructions and operator-assisted installation support targeting completion within seven (7) calendar days of artifact delivery, subject to schedule coordination. Additional emergency install support outside of standard business hours will be provided per the 24x7 support addendum described in Schedule B.

Redwood will supply an offline operator runbook, a signed SBOM snapshot, and access to two (2) ninety-minute live training sessions as part of the Professional Services engagement. Recordings of sessions will be provided for Helios internal use."

If that looks good, Priya, please convert to MAP line items and add estimated cost and SOW language. Attaching MAP.

V.
